headline: Your Food Cost Isn't Just a Purchasing Problem
deck: Price matters. So do waste, portions, overproduction, storage, labor habits and systems that let product disappear without anyone noticing.
author: Josh Freeman
heroImageAlt: Chef reviewing operating notes and kitchen data after service
body: Operators often react to bad food cost by staring harder at invoices. Purchasing matters, but the invoice only tells you what came through the door.

What happens after delivery is where a lot of money disappears: poor rotation, trim loss, oversized portions, unnecessary prep, overproduction, comps, remakes, spoilage and recipes that nobody follows consistently.

The useful question is not only 'what did this cost?' It is 'where did the value go between receiving and the guest?' That turns food cost from a purchasing complaint into an operating problem you can actually investigate.
joshTake: If the first answer to every food-cost problem is 'beat up the vendor,' I assume we have not looked hard enough inside the building yet.
seoTitle: Food Cost Is Not Just a Purchasing Problem
seoDescription: Why restaurant food cost depends on waste, portions, production, storage and operating systems as much as vendor pricing.
